title: Perimeter Policy Fabric: composable Terraform module for SGs, NACLs, private DNS and egress policies
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a composable Terraform module (perimeter-policy-fabric) that standardizes security controls for Private/VPC deployments: security groups (least-privilege presets + managed exceptions), network ACL templates for multi-AZ subnets, private Route53 zone bootstrapping and resolver config, and opinionated egress policy enforcement (allow-lists with centralized proxy/hub support). Module should be reusable across Hosted Dedicated and Private stacks, support cross-account VPC peering and Transit Gateway patterns, and include upgrade-safe migrations for existing customer stacks.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes clear inputs for environment (env), tenancy (shared/dedicated), and role-based presets (control-plane, inference-pool, admin).
Creating a new environment with the module produces idempotent SGs and NACLs with tags and owner metadata compatible with console observability.
Private DNS module registers Route53 private zones and configures inbound/outbound resolver rules when requested; no change to public DNS.
Egress policy supports three enforcement modes: ALLOWLIST_DIRECT, PROXY_HUB, and FALLBACK_ROUTE with automated health-check gating.
Module can be upgraded in-place without causing mass instance restarts; migration plan documented and smoke-tested.
Automated integration tests validate policy enforcement using a test VPC (connectivity matrix), and health checks surface failures to Console.
technical_notes: Design is split into four sub-modules wired by a single root: sg-presets, nacl-templates, pdns-bootstrap, and egress-orchestrator. Each sub-module is separately versioned and publishes upgrade notes. We will avoid provider-specific hacks; prefer stable AWS constructs and use data sources for existing resources to enable safe imports. Use Terraform 1.5+ features (for_each with maps, providers meta) and semantic versioning for module releases. Tagging schema: redwood:component, redwood:owner, redwood:env, redwood:policy_version.
migration_plan: Phase 1: Introduce module in parallel mode with new stacks; Phase 2: Provide terraform import snippets and helper script to map existing SG/NACL resources to module-managed resources; Phase 3: Gradual adopt-by-resource with feature flag in console to opt-in; Phase 4: Deprecate legacy unmanaged policies after 30-day monitoring window. Provide rollback plan that re-applies prior state if breakthrough connectivity regressions occur.
testing_plan: Unit: terratest harness for module outputs and plan diffs. Integration: Provision ephemeral test VPCs in CI with three AZs, deploy module in each egress mode, run connectivity matrix (control-plane->inference, inference->internet, inference->proxy) and assert allowed/blocked flows. Chaos: simulate proxy outage and validate FALLBACK_ROUTE path and Console alert. Security tests: run automated port scans and ensure only expected ports are open.
rollout_plan: 1) Publish v0.1.0 module and docs. 2) Engage two pilot customer teams (Dedicated and Private) to adopt in non-prod. 3) Collect telemetry for 2 weeks, iterate. 4) Offer migration runbook and schedule a cross-team migration week. 5) Mark GA after two successful pilot migrations and security review sign-off.
implementation_steps: Create module scaffold with sub-modules and tf registry metadata.
Implement sg-presets with least-privilege role templates and exception APIs.
Build nacl-templates supporting stateless subnet-level controls and explicit ephemeral port ranges.
Implement pdns-bootstrap to create private zones and resolver rules; add cross-account delegation support.
Develop egress-orchestrator that wires ALLOWLIST and PROXY_HUB modes and exposes health probes endpoints.
Add IAM roles/policies needed by module for resolver automation and Route53 changes with minimal privileges.
Write terratest and CI pipelines and a sample repo demonstrating adoption patterns.
Draft migration scripts and user-facing runbook for Solutions/SE teams.
Coordinate security review and finalize SCA and threat model updates.
blockers: Need consolidated tagging contract from Platform Observability team (TSC-88).
Route53 cross-account delegation requires additional IAM approvals from Security for production domains.
